Hockey Style Paths

Ice hockey 3 vs 3 on a 120 by 60 m rink, seen from behind the player's skater. Three art styles, each as a ladder of three tiers, to compare with the toy diorama baseline from the first set.

Reference studies only. Under contest rule 7(h) these images are never imported into any Unreal project, never used as textures, backdrops or tracing sources, and never shipped. The chosen look is rebuilt from scratch in the engine during the jam. Generated 2026-11-11 with Codex image generation, one image per run, no reference images attached, all nine first try. The subject and camera sentence is identical in all nine, so only the style differs. Feasibility notes assume Unreal Engine 5.9 on one RTX 4090 with agents and about 20 hours of device-B time; they come from general UE 5.x knowledge, and hours and frame times are estimates, not measurements.

Flag. The P4 stills show small blue lettering-like marks on the stick shaft and glove cuff (clearest in T3) that look like a stick maker's mark. Do not show P4 publicly without cropping or regenerating. No real landmark, team, logo or person was seen in P2 or P3.

P2 Painted celP3 Clay miniatureP4 Stylized broadcastComparisonDecide

P2 Painted cel

Hand-painted textures, ink outlines, flat cel steps, five or six colours plus one accent, painted backdrop cards.

Carries the look

Toon ramp in the master materials, one post-process outline pass, painted textures in a small palette, painted backdrop cards that hide the size of the arena.

Costlow

About 8 of 20 hours: toon master and outline 3, painted textures and decals 3, backdrop cards and dressing 2.

Frame-rate risklow

One full-screen post pass plus simple materials. Should hold 60 fps on a GTX 1660 at 1080p.

Third-person effectlow

Outlines keep figures and puck separate from pale ice at any distance. Give the puck a thicker outline or ring; the far net reads as a red outlined box.

Theme bend

Good. A palette swap and new backdrop cards re-theme it, and outlines unify meshes added late.

Designer fit

High. About 80 percent of the look is parameters: palette, ramp steps, outline width, backdrop set.

How the ladder stacks: One toon master and outline pass from T1. T2 swaps the key light and raises emissive trim; T3 adds ray cards, pickup glow and saturation as parameters. No rebuild.

P3 Clay miniature

Matte clay and felt with fingerprint detail, soft rounded forms, warm bounce light, a hint of tilt-shift at the far end.

Carries the look

Texture work: fingerprint normal, felt fuzz from shell cards or a rim trick, stitch decals, high roughness, warm bounce, depth of field.

Costmed

About 12 of 20 hours: materials 4, soft figure meshes with stitching 4, fairy lights and pickups 2, depth of field and puck visibility 2.

Frame-rate riskmed

Cinematic depth of field is a full-screen cost. A simple depth of field should hold 60 fps on a GTX 1660; unshadowed bulbs are cheap.

Third-person effectmed

Depth of field softens the far end, where the far net is. Set focus between player and puck and cap the blur at the net.

Theme bend

Medium to poor. Suits warm toy themes, fights sci-fi or horror; a retheme needs new textures.

Designer fit

Medium. Colour, roughness, blur strength and light colour are parameters; the clay character is in textures and meshes.

How the ladder stacks: One clay and felt material set from T1. T2 dims the room and enables spot cones and trim; T3 adds fairy-light strings and glowing pickups. No rebuild, but the depth-of-field focus rule must exist in T1.

P4 Stylized broadcast

Semi-realistic PBR, glossy boards, scraped ice, glass panels, rig lighting, lens flare and bloom, a sports-broadcast feel.

Carries the look

Stock PBR with glossy ice and scrape decals, glass, rig lights, bloom and flare, Lumen with ray-traced ice reflections. Dressing (stands, crowd, truss) is the heavy part.

Costhigh

About 14 of 20 hours and the highest risk of not finishing: athletes with helmets, visors and animation 5, stands and crowd 3, lights and post 2, ice and glass 2, reflection fallback 2.

Frame-rate riskhigh

Reflections and haze are in the base look from T1. A GTX 1660 has no RT hardware and an RTX 3060 likely drops under 60 fps at 1080p. Needs a reflection quality switch from the start.

Third-person effectmed

Best sports-broadcast feel. At 120 m the stands run 360 m, the far net is tiny and reflections cover the plane; it needs the strongest puck highlight and net beacon.

Theme bend

Medium. Carries sports and arena themes; other themes need new dressing and new athletes.

Designer fit

Medium to low. Light colour, bloom and grade are parameters; the look lives in assets such as stands, athletes and glass.

How the ladder stacks: One PBR set and glossy ice from T1. T2 turns house lights down and spots up; T3 adds neon strips, haze and wet ice. It stacks, but T1 already pays the reflection cost, so the ladder saves less than in P2 or P3.

P1 scores are those of D1 in the first study, with readability lowered one point because the baseline was never imaged from this camera on the large rink. P3 and P4 look best in the stills and cost the most. P2 looks clearly different from the baseline at a similar cost and keeps puck and team readability. In every path the far net is small at 120 m, so the shared kit needs a puck marker and a far-net beacon whichever style wins. Order of risk: P1, P2, P3, P4.
